question: If you see a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane, what must you do?
options: a:The pedestrian must yield the right-of-way.,b:You must yield the right-of-way.,c:Honk your horn to alert them.
note: Pedestrians with guide dogs or white canes are visually impaired and have the right-of-way. Yield and allow them to cross safely.

question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn, where might you expect to see them?
options: a:They may use the left lane.,b:They may cut through all lanes.,c:They may wait on the side of the road.
note: Bicyclists generally follow the same rules as motor vehicles and may use the left lane when preparing to make a left turn.

question: In the event you are about to be struck from the rear, which action should you not do?
options: a:Release your seat belt.,b:Brace yourself.,c:Press your head against the head restraint.
note: Do not release your seat belt. Brace yourself by pressing against the seat back and head restraint and be ready to apply the brakes if possible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, what is the safest action?
options: a:Get out of your vehicle and flag down passing cars.,b:Sound your horn at passing cars to get attention.,c:Pull off the road, turn on emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if possible.
note: If you must stop on the shoulder, use emergency flashers and remain in your vehicle if it is safe. Walking beside a high-speed interstate is very dangerous.

question: Which statement about alcohol in any concentration is true?
options: a:It's a stimulant.,b:It's a depressant.,c:It has no effect on the nervous system.,d:It improves concentration.
note: Alcohol, even in small amounts, acts as a depressant and impairs nerve and bodily functions.

question: When parking facing uphill with no curb, how should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn wheels away from the edge of the road.,b:Turn wheels toward the edge of the road.,c:Keep wheels straight.,d:Turn wheels toward the center of the road.
note: When parking uphill without a curb, turn the front wheels to the right (away from the center) so the vehicle will roll off the road if brakes fail.

question: Because motorcycles and scooters are harder to see, drivers should:
options: a:Share a lane with a motorcycle.,b:Make constant visual checks.,c:Slow down when driving.
note: Motorcycles are small and can easily be missed in a quick glance or in blind spots. Make frequent visual checks to spot them.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what is the first action you should take?
options: a:Ease up on the gas pedal.,b:Brake as hard as possible.,c:Turn off the ignition.
note: When a skid begins, release the accelerator or brake and steer where you want the vehicle to go. Avoid hard braking unless ABS requires otherwise.

question: How should you steer and brake in inclement weather?
options: a:Steer off the road.,b:Drive in a low gear.,c:Steer and brake smoothly.
note: In poor conditions, avoid sudden steering or braking. Smooth, gentle inputs help maintain control on slippery surfaces.

question: How is driving slower than surrounding traffic typically viewed?
options: a:Appropriate if you don’t know the speed limit.,b:Often a hazard because others may try unsafe passes.,c:A good idea if the weather is bad.
note: Driving much slower than the flow of traffic can cause frustration and risky passing maneuvers by other drivers, increasing collision risk.

question: If you feel tired while driving, what is the recommended action?
options: a:Increase the volume of your radio.,b:Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.,c:Increase your speed to reach the destination faster.
note: Warning signs of fatigue include struggling to stay awake or drifting lanes. If you notice these, stop in a safe place and rest or nap.

question: At crosswalks, intersections, and railroad crossings, what should you always do?
options: a:Stop, listen, and proceed cautiously.,b:Slowly pass vehicles that seem to be stopped for no reason.,c:Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
note: Whenever people or other traffic may cross your path, look to the left and right sides of your vehicle to ensure no one is approaching.

question: Why should you avoid using high beams in fog or mist?
options: a:The light will reflect back into your eyes.,b:Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.,c:Approaching vehicles might not see you.
note: High beams reflect off fog and mist, creating glare that reduces visibility for you and other drivers.

question: Alcohol belongs to which drug classification?
options: a:A stimulant.,b:A depressant.,c:An antihistamine.,d:A hallucinogen.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows down the brain and nervous system, impairing judgment and reaction time.

question: Which is a safe driving habit?
options: a:Using your high beam lights in the fog.,b:Staring fixedly at the road ahead.,c:Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.
note: Scan the road and check mirrors every 2–5 seconds to remain aware of hazards. Use low beams in fog, not high beams, and avoid staring at a single spot.

question: If you are angry after an argument, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Loudly play the radio while driving so you won’t think about your argument.,b:Take a few minutes to cool off before driving.,c:Drive on the interstate to let off steam.
note: Emotional distress affects concentration and decision-making; allow time to calm down before operating a vehicle.

question: Which ability is affected first by alcohol?
options: a:Balance.,b:Judgment.,c:Vision.
note: Alcohol first impairs judgment and decision-making, which then affects other driving skills.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it permissible to drive on the shoulder to pass another vehicle?
options: a:If the shoulder is wide enough.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:If the vehicle ahead is turning left.,d:If emergency vehicles are behind you.
note: Never drive on the shoulder to pass; passing on the right is allowed only when it can be done safely without leaving the roadway.

question: What should you do before stopping your vehicle at a traffic signal or sign?
options: a:Press down hard on the accelerator.,b:Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.,c:Set the parking brake.
note: Before braking to stop, check mirrors for traffic around you and apply steady pressure to the brake for a smooth stop.

question: What is the proper way to back up your vehicle?
options: a:Rely only on your rearview mirror.,b:Press hard on the gas pedal.,c:Look directly through the rear window while moving slowly.
note: When reversing, turn and look through the rear window, placing your right arm over the seatback. Do not rely solely on mirrors and go slowly.

question: If you have a sudden tire blowout, what is the safest brake action?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly.,b:Pump the brakes.,c:Use the brakes lightly.
note: Hold the wheel steady, release the accelerator, and slow down gradually—use the brakes lightly once speed has dropped.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning in wet conditions?
options: a:Drive at a speed appropriate for ideal conditions.,b:Apply your brakes as soon as your car starts to skid.,c:Slow down.
note: Reduce speed in wet conditions to maintain tire contact with the road and avoid hydroplaning.

question: When preparing to change lanes, which statement is correct?
options: a:Vehicles with two outside mirrors do not have blind spots.,b:Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and over your left shoulder for a left lane change.,c:You only need to turn and look over your right shoulder for lane changes to the right or left.
note: Before changing lanes, signal, check all mirrors, and look over the shoulder toward the lane you plan to enter to check the blind spot for vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you start a left turn from a multilane, one-way street onto another one-way street?
options: a:Any lane as long as it's safe.,b:The lane closest to the left curb.,c:The lane in the center of the road.
note: When turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, begin from the far left lane and turn into the leftmost lane of the street you're entering.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to make a left turn from a two-way street, where should you position your vehicle?
options: a:Near the right-hand side of the road.,b:Near the centerline.,c:On the left of the centerline.
note: To turn left from a two-way street, position your vehicle near the centerline and begin the turn when it's safe to do so without cutting the corner.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing a vehicle on the left, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:After about three seconds.,b:When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.,c:When you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: Return to the right lane when you can see the passed vehicle's front (headlights) in your rearview mirror and it is safe to do so.

question: When may you legally drive around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate?
options: a:When warning lights are not flashing.,b:When you can see clearly both directions.,c:Never.,d:When traffic is backed up.
note: It is illegal and dangerous to go around or under lowered crossing gates; wait until the gates are raised and it is safe.

question: What restriction applies to all drivers under 21 regarding alcohol?
options: a:They cannot drive after consuming any alcohol.,b:They cannot drive after midnight.,c:They cannot smoke while driving.,d:They cannot drive on highways.
note: Drivers under 21 are prohibited from driving after consuming any alcohol; a zero-tolerance rule applies and violations can suspend licenses.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a pedestrian began crossing after the Don't Walk started and is in the intersection when your light turns green, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.,b:Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing before going.,c:Proceed because you have the right-of-way.,d:Honk and continue carefully.
note: You must yield to pedestrians already in the intersection and wait until they have crossed before proceeding on your green signal.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning on wet roads?
options: a:Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.,b:Put on cruise control.,c:Slow down.,d:Speed up to maintain momentum.
note: Hydroplaning happens when tires lose contact with the road due to water; slow down in wet conditions to reduce the risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach a green light but the intersection is blocked by traffic, what is the best action?
options: a:Partially enter the intersection to establish your right-of-way.,b:Don't enter the intersection until you can get completely across.,c:Continue into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.
note: Do not enter and block the intersection; wait until you can safely clear it before proceeding on a green light.

question: Regulatory signs are typically what color?
options: a:Yellow.,b:White.,c:Green.,d:Red.
note: Regulatory signs inform drivers of laws that must be obeyed (direction, lane use, speed, parking). They are commonly white rectangles or squares with black, red, or green symbols or lettering.

question: Is it appropriate to always drive slower than other traffic?
options: a:No, you may block traffic by driving too slowly.,b:Yes, it's always a good defensive technique.,c:Yes, it's always safer than driving faster than other traffic.
note: While you should reduce speed in poor conditions, driving significantly slower than the flow of traffic can impede traffic and create hazards.

question: If you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you on a city street, what should you do?
options: a:Stay in your lane and slow down.,b:Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.,c:Drive to the right edge and slow down but stay moving.,d:Speed up and get out of the way.
note: Yield to emergency vehicles by pulling to the right edge and stopping until they pass; if in an intersection, clear it first then stop.

question: If you must park in an unusual area, what should you do to reduce hazard?
options: a:Park with your reverse lights on.,b:Make sure your vehicle is visible to drivers approaching from any direction.,c:Park five feet from the curb.
note: Whenever parked, ensure your vehicle is visible to approaching drivers and is not creating a hazard. Use hazard lights if appropriate and legal.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Use your high beam headlights.,b:Use your parking lights.,c:Use your low beam headlights.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and reduce visibility. If visibility is severely reduced, pull off and wait.

question: As your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) rises, what happens to you?
options: a:More sober.,b:More coordinated.,c:More intoxicated.
note: BAC measures the percentage of alcohol in the blood; higher BAC means greater impairment and intoxication.

question: If it feels like your tires have lost contact with the road surface (hydroplaning), what should you do?
options: a:Ease your foot off the gas and avoid braking.,b:Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.,c:Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.,d:Steer sharply to the side of the road.
note: If your tires lose contact with the road, ease off the gas and do not brake or turn until you regain traction. Trying to stop or steer sharply can make the loss of control worse.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to the right lane?
options: a:When you are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.,b:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:When you are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: Return to the right lane only when you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror, indicating you have enough space.

question: What is the only effective way to remove alcohol from your system?
options: a:Drink strong coffee.,b:Wait.,c:Take a cold shower.
note: Time is the only factor that reduces BAC; eating, coffee, or showers do not speed up alcohol elimination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what circumstances may you legally block an intersection?
options: a:If you entered the intersection on a green light.,b:During rush hour traffic.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless you can completely clear it. Blocking intersections is illegal and creates hazards for others.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you treat an intersection controlled by a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Treat it like a stop sign—come to a complete stop, yield, then proceed.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped while the light is red.,d:Treat it the same as a flashing yellow signal.
note: A flashing red signal means stop. After stopping, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when the way is clear.

question: What should you do before entering a curve?
options: a:Activate your turn signal.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Brake hard.
note: Slow down before entering a curve to maintain control and avoid braking sharply while turning.

question: Where should a driver be watching while driving?
options: a:Only directly ahead.,b:Beside, ahead, and behind the vehicle.,c:Only in mirrors.,d:At dashboard instruments.
note: Good driving requires scanning ahead, to the sides, and checking behind to be aware of surrounding hazards.

question: What type of information do blue traffic signs provide?
options: a:Motorist services such as rest areas or hospitals.,b:Construction and maintenance warnings.,c:Mileage to specific locations.
note: Blue signs give service information to motorists, including rest areas, gas, food, and medical facilities.

question: Which headlights are best to use when driving in fog?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Four-way flashers.,c:Fog lights only.,d:Low beam headlights.
note: In fog, rain, or snow use low beam headlights (and fog lights if equipped). High beams reflect back and reduce visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about using a deceleration lane to exit is true?
options: a:Do not use your turn signal until the vehicle has moved into the deceleration lane.,b:Do not follow the posted warning speeds unless the roadway is slippery.,c:Do not slow down until your vehicle has moved into the deceleration lane.
note: Begin slowing only after you have moved into the deceleration lane and continue to slow to the advisory speed for the ramp; do not decelerate abruptly on the mainline.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On the interstate, what is the best way to avoid traffic merging from on-ramps to your right?
options: a:Maintain your speed and position.,b:Slow down.,c:Change lanes to the left when it is safe.
note: When safe and traffic allows, move out of the right-hand lane to allow entering traffic to merge from on-ramps.

question: When another vehicle is passing you, what is the proper action?
options: a:Brake hard.,b:Maintain a constant speed.,c:Speed up.
note: When being passed, maintain a steady speed or slow slightly to allow the other vehicle to pass safely; do not speed up.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If motorists see pedestrians in an upcoming crosswalk, what should they do?
options: a:Pull to the right and go around.,b:Wait for the pedestrians to cross.,c:Proceed since the motorist has right-of-way.,d:Honk to hurry them along.
note: Drivers must yield right-of-way to pedestrians within crosswalks and wait until the crosswalk is clear before proceeding.

question: What is the only proven method to remove alcohol from your system?
options: a:Drink coffee.,b:Give your body time.,c:Take a cold shower.,d:Exercise vigorously.
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize and remove alcohol; coffee, showers, or exercise do not lower BAC.

question: If you begin to feel drowsy while driving, what is the safest action?
options: a:Open a window.,b:Stop and either rest or switch drivers.,c:Drink something with caffeine.
note: To avoid fatigued driving, stop frequently during long trips and rest or change drivers to ensure you are alert.

question: When must you always stop before crossing railroad tracks?
options: a:If there isn't room on the other side to fully clear the tracks.,b:When the crossing is in a busy town.,c:Only if a train is visible.,d:If you are carrying no passengers.
note: Never stop on the tracks; ensure there is enough room to completely clear them before crossing to avoid becoming trapped.

question: What should you remember when driving on gravel or dirt roads?
options: a:Visibility is better than on pavement.,b:Your tires have less traction than on pavement, so you must slow down.,c:Your tires grip the road better than on pavement.
note: Tires have less traction on loose surfaces, so slow down, allow more stopping distance, and avoid sudden turns to reduce skidding.

question: Which of the following removes alcohol and its effects from your body?
options: a:Drinking caffeine.,b:Eating foods high in fat.,c:Time.
note: Only time allows the body to eliminate alcohol and reduce blood alcohol concentration (BAC). No food, drink, or activity will speed this process.

question: What is a likely result of continuous hard braking on ice or snow?
options: a:Helps you stop faster.,b:Locks the front wheels and causes loss of steering.,c:Keeps the brakes from freezing.
note: Hard continuous braking on slippery surfaces can lock the wheels and cause you to lose steering control. Slow and controlled braking is safer; use ABS procedures if equipped.

question: On a slippery road, how should you adjust your following distance?
options: a:No different than normal.,b:Farther than normal.,c:Closer than normal.,d:Only if it's snowing.
note: Increase following distance on slippery surfaces because stopping distances are longer.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action should you never do when changing lanes?
options: a:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,b:Move into another lane while within an intersection.,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
note: Never change lanes while inside an intersection. Before changing lanes, check mirrors and blind spots and signal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a red light with a green arrow, when may you proceed in the arrow's direction?
options: a:You first come to a complete stop.,b:You wait until the light changes.,c:You are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear.
note: If you are in the lane controlled by a green arrow, you may proceed in that direction when the way is clear, yielding to any pedestrians and traffic already in the intersection.

question: In very foggy conditions, what lighting should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Emergency flashers.,c:Low beam headlights.,d:Parking lights only.
note: Use low beam headlights (and fog lights if equipped) in fog to avoid glare from high beams reflecting back.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto the freeway, how fast should you be driving?
options: a:Five to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.,b:At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.,c:At the posted speed limit for freeway traffic.,d:As slow as needed to enter safely.
note: Merge onto the freeway at or near the speed of existing traffic to merge smoothly and safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk, may you pass it?
options: a:You may not pass that vehicle.,b:You may go around if it seems safe.,c:You must honk first.,d:You may pass on the left only.
note: Never pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk; it may be stopped for pedestrians entering the roadway and you must yield to them.

question: If there are oncoming vehicles to your left and parked cars to your right, where should you steer?
options: a:Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.,b:Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.,c:Take a middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.
note: Steer a middle course between oncoming traffic and parked vehicles to avoid sideswipes and opening doors.

question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn where you also plan to turn right, how should you act?
options: a:Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.,b:Quickly turn before the truck or bus is able to.,c:Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn before you turn.
note: Large vehicles may swing wide during turns; do not try to pass between the truck and curb—wait until it completes the turn.

question: What is the primary danger of excessive speed?
options: a:Saves time so you can get to your destination more quickly.,b:Helps you maneuver around obstacles.,c:Increases the likelihood of serious bodily injury and death.
note: Excessive speed is a leading factor in crashes and increases stopping distances and crash severity; it does not save meaningful time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs traffic to go through a red signal, what should you do?
options: a:Stop until the light turns green.,b:Follow the officer's directions and go through the intersection.,c:Come to a complete stop before proceeding.
note: Police officers' instructions override traffic signals and signs; follow their directions for safe traffic flow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes or attempting to pass, what must you do?
options: a:Check your blind spots and mirrors.,b:Signal your intention before changing lanes.,c:All of the above.
note: Always signal before lane changes and check mirrors plus your blind spot by turning your head to ensure the move is safe.

question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Press down on the brake pedal as hard as you can.,b:Slow down gradually and avoid braking heavily.,c:Rapidly pump the brake pedal several times.
note: Grip the steering wheel firmly, take your foot off the gas, and let the vehicle slow. Apply the brakes lightly only if needed and move off the road when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, what checks should you perform to ensure it is safe?
options: a:Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder.,b:Check only the inside rearview mirror.,c:Slow down before changing lanes.
note: Before changing lanes, check mirrors and glance over your shoulder to confirm the lane is clear of vehicles in your blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is unlawful regarding passing?
options: a:Pass another vehicle in any marked no passing zone.,b:Pass another vehicle over a railroad crossing.,c:Both of the above.
note: You may not pass in marked no passing zones, at railroad crossings, on hills or curves where visibility is limited, or when signs prohibit it.

question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change as vehicle speed increases?
options: a:Decrease as a vehicle's speed increases.,b:Are not affected by a vehicle's speed.,c:Increase as a vehicle's speed increases.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distance and the energy in a collision, raising the likelihood of serious injury or death.

question: Why is extra road space needed in front of a large truck?
options: a:So other drivers can merge in front.,b:So the truck driver has room to stop.,c:Because the truck travels slower downhill.,d:To allow the truck to change lanes freely.
note: Large trucks require longer stopping distances; leave extra space so they can brake safely.

question: Which behavior is a likely sign of an aggressive driver?
options: a:The number of passengers in their car.,b:Their erratic and improper lane changes.,c:Their tendency to drive slowly.
note: Aggressive drivers often make erratic or unsafe lane changes and other risky maneuvers. Avoid confronting them and get out of their way.

question: Why is nighttime driving more hazardous than daytime driving?
options: a:You cannot see as far ahead at night.,b:The road is always more slippery at night.,c:Your reaction time is slower at night.
note: Reduced visibility and glare from headlights limit how far you can see at night. Use headlights and drive more cautiously to compensate.

question: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, how must you respond?
options: a:Drive around if no train is visible.,b:Come to a complete stop well behind the gates and wait.,c:Slowly creep under the gates.,d:Proceed if you see only one rail track.
note: It is illegal and unsafe to drive around lowered gates; stop and wait until gates are fully raised and lights stop flashing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?
options: a:When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:When you cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.,c:After signaling for one second.,d:As soon as you pass the front bumper.
note: Return when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror, indicating a safe gap.

question: If a driver is tailgating you on a two-lane road and there is no lane to move into, what should you do?
options: a:Reduce your speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to pass.,b:Speed up to increase the distance between you and the tailgater.,c:Apply your brakes to slow down, then resume your original speed.
note: If you cannot change lanes, gradually slow down to encourage the tailgater to pass or create a safer gap.

question: What is the best general strategy to avoid dangerous driving situations?
options: a:Always keep your eyes focused ahead of your car.,b:Turn off the radio.,c:Know what is happening around your vehicle.
note: Constantly scanning your surroundings—front, sides, and rear—helps you identify hazards early and respond safely.

question: If you see a lane sign showing an arrow with the word 'ONLY' underneath, what must you do?
options: a:Always make a lane change.,b:Look for a destination sign to follow.,c:Travel in the direction of the arrow.
note: Lane control signs with 'ONLY' indicate that traffic in that lane must go in the direction shown by the arrow.

question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the side next to the solid yellow line.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:Passing is permitted from the side next to the broken yellow line.
note: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line means that passing is allowed from the side with the broken line and prohibited from the side with the solid line.

question: When may you cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle?
options: a:If the vehicle in front moves to the right to let you pass.,b:When the yellow line next to your side of the road is broken.,c:If the yellow line on the opposite side is broken.
note: You may cross double lines only when the line nearest your lane is broken, indicating passing is permitted from your side when it is safe.

question: What is a possible effect of taking a prescription drug while drinking alcohol?
options: a:There will likely be no effect.,b:It will make you more alert.,c:It can make you unfit to drive.
note: Mixing alcohol with prescription medications can increase impairment and make driving unsafe or illegal.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline indicate about passing?
options: a:Allowed from both directions.,b:Allowed only from your direction of travel.,c:Not allowed from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines mark opposing traffic where passing is prohibited from either direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a one-way street, you may turn left onto another one-way street only when:
options: a:You increase your speed before the turn.,b:Traffic on the street moves to the right.,c:Traffic on the street moves to the left.
note: You may only turn left onto a one-way street if traffic on that street moves to the left (and no sign prohibits the turn).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at an intersection, whom must you yield to?
options: a:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Only oncoming vehicles.,c:No one, you have the right-of-way.,d:Only vehicles on your right.
note: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming vehicles and to any pedestrians crossing the roadway.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian?
options: a:Only if they are in a crosswalk.,b:Only if the traffic lights favor the pedestrian.,c:At all times, even if the pedestrian is not obeying traffic laws.
note: You must do everything possible to avoid striking a pedestrian. Give pedestrians the right-of-way whenever necessary to prevent a collision.

question: What do 'No passing zone' signs indicate to drivers?
options: a:To speed up slightly.,b:That it is not safe to pass.,c:To maintain a steady speed.
note: A No Passing Zone sign marks an area where it is illegal and unsafe to pass another vehicle.

question: What should you do when the roadway is wet or icy?
options: a:Drive at the posted speed.,b:Speed up.,c:Reduce your speed.
note: Tires have less traction on wet, snowy, or icy roads, so you should slow down to maintain control and stop safely.

question: When must drivers yield right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:Only if the pedestrians first wave to the driver.,b:Only if the pedestrians are not texting while walking.,c:At all times.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians already in a crosswalk or intersection; stop completely if necessary.

question: What risk does fatigue pose while driving?
options: a:Missing an exit.,b:Being late for an appointment.,c:Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.
note: Fatigue reduces alertness and increases the risk of falling asleep at the wheel, which can cause serious crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to drive faster than the posted speed limit?
options: a:Never.,b:If you feel it is reasonable and prudent.,c:When passing another vehicle.
note: The posted speed limit is the maximum allowed. Driving faster than the posted limit is illegal regardless of circumstances.

question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing red light, what must a driver do?
options: a:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, then proceed.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped as long as the light is red.
note: A flashing red light should be treated like a stop sign: stop completely, yield, and proceed only when safe.

question: On a green arrow signal, what must you do before turning?
options: a:Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.,b:Wait four seconds before turning.,c:Only yield to vehicles.,d:Turn immediately without checking.
note: A green arrow permits the turn but requires yielding to any vehicles, cyclists, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

question: When should you allow extra following distance behind another vehicle?
options: a:When following a station wagon.,b:When following a driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle.,c:When following a small passenger car.
note: Give extra space behind large vehicles or those towing trailers because the driver may have limited rear visibility and might need to stop or maneuver.

question: If your vehicle has ABS and you must stop on snow or ice, what should you do with the brake pedal?
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,c:Stay off the brakes and wait for the car to drift to a stop.
note: With an Anti-Lock Braking System, press and hold the brake pedal firmly. The system will automatically modulate braking to prevent wheel lockup.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the legal status of texting while driving?
options: a:Permitted if driving at a slow speed.,b:Not legal.,c:Legal if the driver is 21 years of age or older.
note: Texting while driving is illegal and considered highly distracting; Maryland law prohibits using handheld devices while driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you face a green light but the intersection is blocked by traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Turn left and find another route.,b:Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.,c:Follow the other vehicles and enter the intersection.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it completely; entering and blocking it can result in a citation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?
options: a:It is illegal to turn off your signal before completing a turn.,b:It notifies other drivers of your intended actions.,c:It is always unsafe to turn off a signal before completing a turn.
note: Signaling informs other road users of your intended maneuver, helping to prevent conflicts and accidents.

question: Where are large trucks' blind spots commonly located?
options: a:On the immediate left of the cab.,b:Directly behind the body.,c:Both on the immediate left of the cab and directly behind the body.
note: Trucks have large blind spots on both the left side of the cab and directly behind the trailer. If you cannot see the truck driver in their mirror, the truck driver likely cannot see you.

question: Which statement about blind spots is accurate?
options: a:They are eliminated if you have one outside mirror on each side of the vehicle.,b:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,c:Blind spots can be checked by looking in your rearview mirrors.
note: Blind spots are areas not visible in mirrors; large trucks have much larger blind spots that other drivers should avoid.

question: What does a steady red arrow on a traffic light mean?
options: a:Drivers must come to a full stop and may not proceed in the arrow's direction.,b:Drivers may turn after stopping.,c:Drivers should speed up to clear the intersection.,d:Drivers may turn if clear.
note: A steady red arrow prohibits movement in the indicated direction; drivers must stop and wait for a green signal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement is true about driving too slowly on highways?
options: a:Driving too slowly is not an unsafe practice.,b:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,c:The speed at which you drive a vehicle does not affect safety.
note: Driving much slower than the flow of traffic can cause congestion and risky passing maneuvers; drive with the flow when safe and lawful.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach an intersection with a steady yellow light and haven't entered it, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Come to a safe stop if you can.,c:Drive through regardless.,d:Stop in the middle of the intersection.
note: A steady yellow warns the light is about to turn red; if you can stop safely, do so rather than running the red light.

question: What is the purpose of broken yellow lines on streets and highways?
options: a:Indicate no passing zones.,b:Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.,c:Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.
note: Broken yellow centerlines separate opposing traffic and indicate that passing is permitted when it is safe to do so.

question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, what should you do?
options: a:Switch to high beams.,b:Turn your lights on and off.,c:Look toward the right edge of the road.,d:Close your eyes briefly.
note: Glance toward the right edge of the roadway to avoid being blinded while keeping your vehicle safely positioned.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You enter a left-turn lane and there is oncoming traffic. What should you do before turning?
options: a:Turn your front wheels to the left to be prepared to turn.,b:Signal before you arrive at the intersection.,c:Move to the left of the center lane.
note: Signal about 100 feet before turning and keep your wheels straight until it's safe to turn to avoid being pushed into oncoming traffic if hit from behind.

question: If dust or smoke reduces visibility, what lighting should you use?
options: a:Emergency flashers.,b:Parking lights.,c:Headlights.
note: Turn on your headlights when conditions reduce visibility so other drivers can see you. Use low beams rather than high beams in dust or smoke.

question: How should you react to a flashing yellow light at an intersection?
options: a:Stop, then proceed when clear.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Yield to all traffic before crossing.,d:Ignore it and go normally.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down, be alert for cross traffic, and proceed carefully without stopping unless necessary.

question: What does the acronym BAC stand for?
options: a:Blood alcohol concentration.,b:Big alcohol content.,c:Blood alcohol conservation.
note: BAC measures the percentage of alcohol in a person's bloodstream; 0.08% or higher is the legal limit for drivers 21 and older.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle approaching with flashing lights, how must you respond?
options: a:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it has passed.,b:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane until it has passed.,c:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it has passed.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights or siren, pull to the right edge of the road and stop until it has passed, yielding as required.

question: A broken yellow centerline next to your lane indicates what about passing?
options: a:Passing is not permitted.,b:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,c:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow line next to your lane means you may cross to pass when it is safe to do so and there is no oncoming traffic.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, what is the safest course of action?
options: a:Pump the brakes rapidly.,b:Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the roadway.,c:Grip the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of the travel lane.
note: Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator to slow gradually, and steer straight until you can safely leave the travel lane and stop.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?
options: a:Passing is not permitted.,b:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,c:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow centerline means you may cross to pass on the left when there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When crossing a sidewalk to enter the roadway from an alley, driveway, or parking lot, what must a driver do?
options: a:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.,b:Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.,c:Expect pedestrians on the sidewalk to yield the right-of-way.,d:Sound your horn and proceed slowly.
note: When leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot, you must stop before entering the sidewalk area. Pedestrians and traffic on the roadway have the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you respond to a traffic signal that is flashing yellow?
options: a:Maintain your normal speed.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop at the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow light warns you to be alert and to proceed with caution. Reduce your speed when approaching and pass carefully.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn the front wheels?
options: a:Straight ahead,b:Right, toward the side of the road,c:Left, toward the center of the road
note: When parking downhill with no curb, turn the front wheels toward the road edge so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where vehicles arrive simultaneously from the right and left, to whom should you yield?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your left.,b:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your right.,c:Wait until there are no vehicles at the intersection before proceeding.
note: At uncontrolled intersections, yield to the vehicle on your right when multiple vehicles arrive at the same time.

question: When changing lanes, what visual check is required?
options: a:Rely on the rearview mirror.,b:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,c:Rely on the left side mirror.
note: Glance over your shoulder in the direction of the lane change to check the blind spot in addition to using mirrors and signals.

question: Which action should you never do when changing lanes?
options: a:Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,b:Change lanes abruptly or spontaneously.,c:Check for other vehicles moving into the same lane.
note: Avoid making sudden, unindicated lane changes; always signal, check mirrors, and look over your shoulder before moving.

question: If there is a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline, what does it mean?
options: a:Do not pass.,b:Traffic light ahead.,c:Reduce your speed.
note: A solid yellow line on your side indicates that passing is prohibited from your lane.

question: What should you do to reduce the risk of hydroplaning in rainy conditions?
options: a:Put on your cruise control to maintain a constant speed.,b:Move to the shoulder of the road as soon as it starts to rain.,c:Decrease your speed.
note: Reduce speed in wet conditions to keep your tires in contact with the road. High speeds can cause your tires to ride on a film of water, causing loss of control.

question: Any amount of alcohol in your bloodstream can impair which of the following?
options: a:Knowledge.,b:Right-of-way privileges.,c:Judgment and physical coordination.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol can affect your judgment and physical coordination. Impairment can occur below legal limits and may lead to criminal charges.

question: How should you respond to a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane?
options: a:You must tell them where to cross the street.,b:You must always yield the right-of-way.,c:You only have to yield if you are at a corner.
note: Blind or partially blind pedestrians using a guide dog or white cane must always be yielded the right-of-way by drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is close enough to cause a conflict.,b:Yield only to vehicles on your right.,c:Slow down but never stop.
note: At a yield sign you must slow or stop as necessary and yield to crossing or merging traffic that is close enough to be a hazard.

question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means which vehicles may pass?
options: a:Driving in both directions may pass.,b:Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.,c:Vehicles next to the solid line may pass.
note: If the broken line is adjacent to your lane, you may pass when it is safe. The solid line indicates the opposite direction may not pass.

question: What attitude should you have when driving in a construction zone?
options: a:Slightly increase your speed.,b:Expect the unexpected.,c:Expect workers to yield to motorists.
note: Construction zones often present sudden lane changes, workers, and equipment. Drive cautiously and be prepared for unexpected conditions.

question: What message will be displayed on a red octagon-shaped sign?
options: a:Do not enter.,b:Stop.,c:One-way.
note: An octagonal red sign always means STOP. You must come to a complete stop at a stop sign before proceeding.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim their headlights, what is the best action for you to take?
options: a:Turn on your high beams to signal them.,b:Look toward the right side of the road.,c:Look toward the center of the roadway.,d:Keep looking straight ahead.
note: If an oncoming driver does not dim high beams, look toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded while keeping track of your lane position. Do not retaliate with your high beams.

question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, what should you expect?
options: a:The child to be fully in control.,b:The unexpected from the child.,c:That honking will correct behavior.,d:That the child will always stop at intersections.
note: Children can be unpredictable on bicycles; be alert and expect sudden movements to avoid a collision.

question: When should you increase the space between your vehicle and the one ahead?
options: a:When you are following a small passenger vehicle.,b:When you are being tailgated by another driver.,c:When you are driving more slowly than the posted speed limit.
note: If another driver is tailgating you, create extra space ahead to reduce the risk of a collision and avoid braking suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How do you know it's safe to return to your lane after passing another car?
options: a:If the other driver signals for you to re-enter the lane.,b:If you look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you.,c:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: Only return to your lane when you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror; also check your blind spot before moving over.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:At any intersection where a police officer orders you to stop.,b:At a red traffic light.,c:Both of the above.,d:Only at stop signs.
note: You must obey traffic signals like steady/flashing red lights and any direction given by officers directing traffic.

question: Before starting the engine, which safety action should you take?
options: a:Buckle your safety belt.,b:Be sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.,c:Both of the above.
note: Develop a routine: before switching on the ignition, fasten your seat belt and ensure passengers are buckled.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you drive at the posted maximum speed limit?
options: a:At night.,b:Only under ideal conditions.,c:During rain.,d:Whenever the driver wants.
note: Posted maximum speeds are the fastest safe speed under ideal conditions; adjust speed lower for hazards, traffic, and weather.

question: Like drugs or alcohol, what effect can drowsiness have on driving?
options: a:Improve awareness.,b:Make you feel better.,c:Impair your judgment.,d:Increase reaction speed.
note: Drowsiness impairs judgment, slows reaction time, and reduces awareness similar to alcohol or drug impairment.

question: How can you keep track of traffic behind you?
options: a:Turn and look out your back window.,b:Frequently check your rearview mirror.,c:Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.
note: Regularly check your rearview mirror to be aware of following traffic and potential hazards behind you.

question: If the rear of your vehicle skids left, how should you steer to correct it?
options: a:Not turn your steering wheel.,b:Turn your steering wheel to the left to correct the skid.,c:Turn your steering wheel to the right to correct the skid.
note: When the rear of the vehicle skids left, steer in the same direction as the skid (left) to help regain control. With ABS, apply brakes firmly and steer straight if appropriate.

question: To help others see you as daylight fades, what lights should you use?
options: a:Parking lights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Emergency flashers.,d:High beam headlights.
note: Turn on low beam headlights as daylight fades to increase visibility to other road users; reserve high beams where no other traffic is present.

question: If you approach a stopped emergency vehicle using visual signals, what should you do?
options: a:Increase your speed to get around the incident quickly.,b:Ask the emergency workers if they need your help.,c:Move into the lane farthest from the vehicle or slow down.
note: If an emergency vehicle is stopped with visual signals, move over to a non-adjacent lane if possible; otherwise slow down to a safe speed and be prepared to stop.

question: Why should drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?
options: a:They do not have the same physical reflexes as adults.,b:They are smaller and more difficult to see than adults.,c:Both of the above.
note: Children are less predictable and harder to see; give them extra room near schools, parks, and residential areas.

question: If you've had several beers, how can the alcohol effects be reduced?
options: a:Drinking several cups of coffee.,b:Waiting several hours.,c:Taking a cold shower.
note: Only time removes alcohol from your system; remedies like coffee, exercise, or cold showers do not reduce BAC.

question: If a stopped school bus ahead in your lane has red lights flashing, how long must you remain stopped?
options: a:Stop and proceed when you think all of the children have exited the bus.,b:Slow to 25 mph and pass cautiously.,c:Stop for as long as the red lights are flashing.
note: When approaching a stopped school bus with flashing red lights, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a left turn from a one-way street, which lane should you be in?
options: a:The lane nearest the center of the street.,b:The lane nearest the right curb.,c:The lane nearest the left curb.,d:Any lane as long as it is clear.
note: When turning, start from the lane closest to the direction you intend to travel. On a one-way street, a left turn should be made from the lane nearest the left curb into the first legal lane.

question: Why use headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?
options: a:To warn others of bad weather conditions.,b:To keep your engine warm.,c:So others can see your vehicle.
note: Headlights make your vehicle more visible to others in poor weather; when wipers are needed, low beams must also be used.

question: Why is slowing down to look at crashes or odd events discouraged?
options: a:It causes traffic congestion.,b:It prevents rear-end collisions.,c:It improves traffic flow.,d:It helps emergency responders.
note: Slowing to look ('rubbernecking') creates congestion and can cause additional collisions; keep moving safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How can you check a blind spot when changing lanes?
options: a:Using the inside rearview mirror.,b:Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.,c:Using your side mirror.
note: Turn your head to look over your shoulder to view areas not visible in mirrors before changing lanes.

question: How should you respond to a flashing yellow traffic signal?
options: a:Wait for the green light before proceeding.,b:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.,c:Stop before crossing the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down, be cautious, and proceed through the intersection with care, watching for other traffic and pedestrians.

question: If you approach a steady yellow traffic signal and have not entered the intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.,c:Come to a safe stop.
note: A steady yellow means the light is about to turn red. If you can stop safely before the intersection, do so.

question: In fog, rain, or snow which headlights are appropriate to use?
options: a:Low beams.,b:High beams.,c:Fog lights only.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow because high beams create glare; fog lights may be used in addition where fitted.

question: If you park facing uphill on a street with a curb, how should you turn the front wheels?
options: a:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,c:Leave the front wheels straight.
note: When parked uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb if the brakes fail.

question: Which type of roadway is most likely to be icy in cold weather after precipitation?
options: a:A hilly, open road,b:A residential road,c:A road in a shaded area.
note: Shaded areas freeze before and thaw after the rest of the road, making them especially likely to be icy after snow or rain.

question: If you see pedestrians near the roadway, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn and maintain your speed.,b:Speed up to clear the area quickly.,c:Slow down and pass with caution.
note: Slow down and be prepared to stop; pedestrians near the road may step into your path unexpectedly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How can you make room for cars entering the freeway?
options: a:Maintaining your speed and position.,b:Merging into a different lane when possible.,c:Slowing down only if someone honks at you.
note: When possible and safe, change lanes to create gaps; if you cannot, adjust speed so entering vehicles can merge smoothly.

question: How are stopping distances and crash severity affected by higher speeds?
options: a:Are not affected by vehicle speed.,b:Decrease as vehicle speed increases.,c:Increase as vehicle speed increases.
note: Higher speeds lengthen stopping distances and increase the severity of crashes—including risk of serious injury or death.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the driver ahead stops at a crosswalk, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and wait until pedestrians have cleared.,b:Cautiously pass at 10 mph.,c:Change lanes and pass immediately.,d:Honk and go around them.
note: Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk; there may be pedestrians crossing that you cannot see until you stop.

question: Why is night driving more hazardous?
options: a:The speed limit is increased at night.,b:There are fewer cars on the roads at night.,c:Distance and vehicle speed are difficult to judge in the dark.
note: Reduced visibility at night makes it harder to judge distance and speed of other vehicles; you can only see as far as your headlights allow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When facing a green light and pedestrians are in the intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.,b:Proceed since you have the green.,c:Sound your horn and continue.,d:Speed up to clear the intersection first.
note: Yield to pedestrians who are in the intersection before you proceed, even on a green signal.

question: When passing a motorcycle, what must you ensure?
options: a:Have your vehicle fully in the left lane before and during the pass.,b:Blow your horn and pass closely.,c:Allow the motorcycle a full lane and do not crowd it.,d:Pass on the shoulder if the lane is narrow.
note: Give motorcycles a full lane; do not share the lane or crowd them, and ensure you are fully in the passing lane before returning.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.,c:Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.
note: A flashing yellow means exercise caution and proceed when safe; it does not require a full stop.

question: What must you do when you approach an intersection with a flashing red light?
options: a:Slow down and yield the right-of-way.,b:Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.,c:Come to a complete stop, check traffic, and go when safe.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign: stop completely, yield to vehicles and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If pedestrians are illegally crossing mid-street, how should you respond?
options: a:You must stop for them.,b:You do not have to stop.,c:Honk and proceed.,d:Drive around them slowly.
note: You must yield to pedestrians in the roadway even if they are not using a crosswalk; stop and let them cross safely.

question: What does a yellow left-turn arrow signal indicate?
options: a:The protected left turn is about to end.,b:Yield to pedestrians only.,c:Stop and wait.,d:Left turns are prohibited.
note: A yellow arrow warns that the protected left-turn phase is ending and drivers should prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.

question: When in a work zone, what following distance practice should you follow?
options: a:Follow closely to the driver ahead.,b:Avoid tailgating and maintain a safe following distance.,c:Pass as soon as possible.,d:Ride the bumper to prevent merging.
note: Keep an increased following distance in work zones to allow for sudden stops and changing conditions.

question: How must you yield the right-of-way to an emergency vehicle using siren and flashing lights?
options: a:Stopping immediately, even if you are within an intersection.,b:Drive as closely to the right edge of the road as possible and stop.,c:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it has passed.
note: Yield by pulling to the right edge of the road and stopping; avoid stopping in an intersection. Resume driving after the emergency vehicle has passed.

question: What does a flashing red traffic light at an intersection require you to do?
options: a:The same thing as a yield sign.,b:The light is about to turn green.,c:The same thing as a stop sign.
note: A flashing red light requires a complete stop, yielding as necessary, then proceeding when the way is clear—same as a stop sign.

question: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line means what?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line.,b:Passing is not permitted from either lane.,c:Passing is permitted only from the lane next to the solid line.,d:Both lanes may pass anytime.
note: When a broken yellow line is next to your lane, you may pass when safe; traffic next to the solid line may not pass.

question: If you encounter a flooded roadway, what is the safest action?
options: a:Slam on the brakes.,b:Turn around and find another route.,c:Drive only in the center of the roadway.
note: Do not attempt to drive through flooded areas. Water depth and road damage can be deceptive; turn around and take an alternate route.

question: Is it legal to have open alcoholic containers in a vehicle on a highway?
options: a:Legal if only passengers drink.,b:Illegal to possess or drink from open containers in a vehicle.,c:Legal if the driver is not drunk.,d:Legal when parked on the shoulder.
note: Maryland law prohibits drivers and passengers from possessing open containers of alcohol while the vehicle is being operated.

question: Which factor affects how alcohol is absorbed into the body?
options: a:Weight,b:Height,c:Intelligence
note: Alcohol absorption is affected by factors such as body weight, biological sex, food in the stomach, and how much was consumed.

question: Why avoid sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses?
options: a:They require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.,b:Small vehicles cannot see trucks in rearview mirrors.,c:Large vehicles travel faster.,d:They can swerve more quickly.
note: Large vehicles need more distance to stop; sudden stops in front of them may prevent them from stopping in time.

question: What do yellow centerlines on the pavement indicate?
options: a:All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.,b:Traffic lanes on one-way streets.,c:Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
note: Yellow centerlines mark the center of a roadway with traffic traveling in opposite directions. A solid yellow centerline means no passing; a broken yellow centerline means passing is allowed when it is safe.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, what is the correct immediate response?
options: a:Apply the brake and hold it.,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly and use the brakes lightly.,c:Pull over quickly.
note: If a tire fails, hold the steering wheel firmly to maintain direction, take your foot off the gas, slow gradually, and apply brakes lightly only if necessary before pulling off the road.

question: What is the only thing that can lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drinking caffeine.,b:Eating foods high in fat.,c:Time.
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize and reduce BAC; no food, drink, or activity will speed this up.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a two-lane road, what should you be sure to do?
options: a:Flash your headlights as you pass.,b:Sound your horn as you pass.,c:Judge the distance and speed of any oncoming vehicles.
note: Ensure there is enough time and distance to pass safely by judging oncoming traffic; wait if you are unsure of speeds.

question: When you come to a flashing red traffic light, what must you do?
options: a:Are traveling in the wrong direction.,b:May not proceed until it changes to green.,c:Treat the intersection as if there is a stop sign.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign: come to a full stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.

question: If your vehicle's wheels have run off the pavement edge, what is the correct first action?
options: a:Turn the front wheels sharply to the left to get back on the pavement.,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas, and gently apply the brakes.,c:Turn the front wheels slightly to the left to edge the car back onto the pavement.
note: Hold the wheel steady, ease off the gas, and gently brake to reduce speed before checking traffic and returning to the road gradually.

question: If the rear of your vehicle skids to the left, what should you do?
options: a:Steer to the right.,b:Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.,c:Steer to the left.
note: Take your foot off the brake or accelerator and steer in the direction you want the front wheels to go. If the rear skids left, steer left to regain control.

question: What should you do when roads are slippery after rain begins?
options: a:Avoid fast turns and stops.,b:Decrease look-ahead distance.,c:Test tires' traction by accelerating uphill.,d:Increase speed to shorten travel time.
note: On newly wet roads, reduce speed and avoid sudden turns or stops to preserve tire traction and reduce skids.

question: When should you not use your horn?
options: a:To warn someone you might hit.,b:Near blind pedestrians.,c:When visibility ahead is limited.,d:To alert drivers of a danger.
note: Do not use your horn around blind pedestrians; it may confuse them. Yield and proceed only when safe.

question: What does 'implied consent' require of drivers in Maryland?
options: a:You will submit to a physical examination before licensure.,b:You will submit to a field sobriety test to determine impairment.,c:You must submit to a requested chemical test to determine your BAC.
note: By driving in Maryland, you consent to submit to chemical testing for alcohol or controlled substances when lawfully requested by an officer.

question: A driver who has been drinking is more likely to have which impairment?
options: a:Yield right-of-way to emergency vehicles.,b:Keep a three to four second following distance.,c:Slower reaction time.,d:Increased alertness.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol can slow reaction time and impair vision and motor skills, increasing crash risk.

question: When driving near a large commercial vehicle, what is a safe practice?
options: a:Follow the large vehicle closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.,b:Avoid driving beside it for long stretches of time.,c:Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.
note: Large commercial vehicles have sizable blind spots; avoid lingering alongside them and pass quickly and safely when necessary.

question: What should you do to prepare yourself and your vehicle before driving?
options: a:Adjust the seat to a reclining position.,b:Kick the tires.,c:Properly adjust your seat and mirrors.
note: Before driving, ensure you have the appropriate license/permit and registration, and adjust your seat and mirrors for proper control and visibility. Ensure all occupants are belted.

question: When should you wear a seat belt while in a vehicle?
options: a:Only on long trips.,b:All the time.,c:Only on high-speed highways.,d:Only when driving at night.
note: Maryland law requires drivers and front-seat passengers to wear seat belts at all times; passengers under 16 must be restrained regardless of seat.

question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?
options: a:Motorcycles do not follow traffic rules.,b:They can stop much quicker than cars.,c:They brake more slowly than cars.,d:They are heavier than cars.
note: Motorcycles can stop quickly; following too closely reduces your time to react and increases collision risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, what should you do before merging onto the interstate?
options: a:Immediately enter the far-right traffic lane on the interstate and speed up to match traffic.,b:Use the shoulder of the main road to get up to the speed of traffic.,c:Speed up and enter the interstate only after you have identified a gap in traffic.
note: On a short ramp without an acceleration lane, wait for a safe gap before entering and then accelerate to match traffic speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, you should move back into your original lane when:
options: a:You are 50 feet in front of the passed vehicle.,b:You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:You have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.,d:The other driver signals you to move back into the lane.
note: Only return to your original lane after passing when you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror, which ensures you have enough space to pull in front safely.

question: At what speed should you travel under varying conditions?
options: a:At the speed of vehicles surrounding you.,b:At the speed limit.,c:At a speed appropriate for road and weather conditions.
note: Drive at a speed that is safe for current road, weather, and traffic conditions while not exceeding the posted limit.

question: Which of these substances can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:Tranquilizers, marijuana, and sedatives.,b:Cough syrups and cold tablets containing codeine or antihistamines.,c:All of the above.
note: Both prescription and over-the-counter medications, as well as illegal drugs, can impair driving ability.

question: What should you do when driving on a slippery surface such as snow or ice?
options: a:Maintain close following behind the vehicle ahead.,b:Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.,c:Shift to a low gear before descending steep hills.
note: On slippery roads, shift to a lower gear before descending steep hills to maintain traction and avoid excessive braking. Increase following distance and brake gently.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To safely enter a gap in highway traffic, what is the correct procedure?
options: a:Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.,b:Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead and the gap.,c:Speed up and let other vehicles make way.
note: Before entering traffic, check behind, to the sides, and watch the vehicle ahead to ensure the gap is large enough to merge safely.

question: When must you obey a school crossing guard's directions?
options: a:At all times.,b:Only during school hours.,c:Only when children are present.
note: Drivers must obey instructions from school crossing guards at all times, not just during school hours or only when children are visible.

question: What do double yellow centerline markings indicate about passing?
options: a:Allowed from both directions.,b:Allowed only from your direction.,c:Not allowed from either direction.
note: Double yellow centerlines mean passing across the lines is prohibited for traffic in both directions.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal indicate?
options: a:You should speed up so you can make the turn before the light changes.,b:You do not need to signal to turn from the indicated lane.,c:You should prepare to stop and yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic.
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protection of a green arrow is ending—prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to exit the interstate, when should you start slowing?
options: a:Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.,b:About halfway through the deceleration lane.,c:As you approach the deceleration lane.,d:Before you see the exit sign.
note: Reduce speed once you enter the deceleration lane and follow the exit ramp advisory speed to leave the freeway safely.

question: What is the purpose of rumble strips along the roadway?
options: a:Alert inattentive drivers through vibration and sound.,b:Test a vehicle's shock absorbers.,c:Warn drivers of tire problems.,d:Provide decorative road texture.
note: Rumble strips create vibrations and noise to warn drivers they are leaving the travel lane or approaching an intersection.

question: If your car's suspension is worn, what problem can result?
options: a:Vehicle control problems.,b:Squealing brakes.,c:Slack in the steering.
note: Bad suspension can cause handling and control issues and should be inspected and repaired to maintain safe control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering an intersection, in what order should you scan for traffic?
options: a:Look to your right.,b:Look to your left.,c:Look left, then right, then left again.
note: Before entering an intersection, look both ways for vehicles and pedestrians. Look to your left a second time because traffic from that direction is usually closer. Also look across the intersection to ensure the way is clear.

question: Which driving behavior most blocks the smooth flow of traffic?
options: a:Slowing down to look at a collision scene.,b:Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.,c:Using public transportation instead of your vehicle.
note: 'Rubbernecking' (slowing to look at incidents) disrupts traffic flow and increases congestion and crash risk.

question: When is it appropriate to sound your horn?
options: a:Another driver makes a mistake.,b:Another vehicle is in your way.,c:When it may help prevent a collision.
note: Use the horn only to warn others and help avoid collisions—not to express frustration.

question: In heavy fog, what is the correct approach to driving?
options: a:Turn on high beam headlights.,b:Increase your speed so you clear the fog quickly.,c:Slow down and use low beam headlights.
note: Reduce speed and use low beam headlights in fog. If visibility becomes extremely poor, pull off the road and wait for conditions to improve.

question: What does a curb painted red indicate?
options: a:A loading zone.,b:Reserved for picking up or dropping off passengers.,c:No parking, standing, or stopping.
note: A red-painted curb means stopping, standing, or parking is prohibited at that location.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Only when a crossing guard is present.,b:Only when the guide dog is leading the person across the street.,c:At all times.
note: Pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog must be given the right-of-way at all times.

question: If you encounter a deep puddle ahead, what is the best action?
options: a:Shift into neutral as you drive through the water.,b:Avoid the puddle if possible.,c:Maintain the posted speed to make it through the water.
note: Avoid deep puddles when possible to reduce the risk of hydroplaning and water-related vehicle damage.

question: When during rainy weather should you be most cautious about turning or stopping?
options: a:One half hour after it stops raining.,b:After it has been raining all day.,c:During the first half hour of rain.
note: The first half hour of rain is especially slippery because oil and residue on the roadway mix with water, reducing traction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is your obligation to pedestrians at a crosswalk?
options: a:You must yield to pedestrians.,b:Pedestrians must yield to vehicles.,c:Construction workers must yield to you.,d:Pedestrians only yield when lights are present.
note: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crossings; vehicles must stop for pedestrians in crosswalks and follow traffic control signals.

question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, what should you expect?
options: a:Slow down because the lane ends ahead.,b:Change lanes and maintain your current speed.,c:Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead.
note: Work-zone signs indicate workers, equipment, or lane closures. Reduce speed and be ready to slow or stop as directed.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is correct?
options: a:You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.,b:You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger or stop sign.,c:You should put on your cruise control near a railroad crossing to maintain a constant speed.
note: You must stop at railroad crossings when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal; always use caution near tracks.

question: What should you do to avoid losing traction on wet roads?
options: a:Make abrupt turns.,b:Apply the brakes firmly.,c:Slow down.
note: Slow down on wet roads to reduce the risk of hydroplaning and maintain control. If traction is lost, ease off the gas and steer smoothly to regain control.

question: How should you behave when approaching a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Carefully drive around them.,b:Honk as a warning and proceed.,c:Stop until the person is clear of your path.,d:Pass closely at low speed.
note: Yield fully to blind pedestrians using aids; stop until they are well clear of your vehicle's path.

question: On a roadway marked with a single broken white centerline, what is permitted?
options: a:You must stay within your lane.,b:You may cross the centerline to change lanes.,c:You may change lanes only from the left lane.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and permit lane changes when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer signals you to stop while the traffic signal is green, what should you do?
options: a:Do what the vehicle in front of you does.,b:Obey the traffic signal.,c:Obey the officer.
note: An officer's directions take precedence over traffic signals and signs; you must follow their instructions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these is unsafe behavior on an interstate?
options: a:Slower traffic keeping to the right.,b:Changing lanes without signaling.,c:If you miss your exit, proceed to the next exit.
note: Always signal before changing lanes. On interstates, slower traffic should stay in the right lanes and you must continue to the next exit if you miss yours.

question: At what speeds can a car begin to hydroplane on standing water?
options: a:40 miles per hour.,b:35 miles per hour.,c:45 miles per hour.
note: Hydroplaning can begin at speeds around or above 35 mph on standing water, when tires can no longer channel water away and lose road contact.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
options: a:Alertness.,b:Coordination.,c:Both of the above.
note: Alcohol and drugs impair multiple skills important to driving, including alertness, coordination, reaction time, and judgment.

question: What does a red arrow pointing right on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Turn in that direction after slowing and checking for traffic.,b:Not turn in that direction until the light turns green.,c:Turn in that direction after you come to a complete stop.
note: A red arrow means you must stop and may not turn in the arrow’s direction until a green signal or green arrow appears.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you never do when changing lanes?
options: a:Check blind spots by looking over your shoulder.,b:Cross the centerline in an intersection.,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.,d:Signal your intent.
note: Never change lanes or pass in an intersection; always check mirrors, your blind spots, and signal before moving.

question: What do double solid yellow lane markings indicate?
