options: a:Neither lane may pass.,b:Both lanes may pass.,c:The lane to the right may pass.
note: Double solid yellow lines between lanes indicate that passing is prohibited for traffic in both directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the best way to change lanes?
options: a:Quickly and often.,b:When a car is in your blind spot.,c:Gradually and carefully.
note: Change lanes slowly and carefully, checking mirrors and blind spots and signaling to ensure the maneuver is safe.

question: If an oncoming vehicle's bright headlights affect your vision at night, what should you do?
options: a:Stop until the other driver passes.,b:Look below their headlights.,c:Glance toward the right edge of your lane.
note: Avoid looking directly at oncoming high beams. Glance toward the right edge of the road and watch the vehicle with peripheral vision until it passes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What approach should a driver take regarding right-of-way rules?
options: a:Assume all drivers obey right-of-way rules.,b:Assume most drivers obey right-of-way rules.,c:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way to avoid collisions.
note: Because other drivers may not follow the rules, be prepared to yield your legal right-of-way when doing so will prevent a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to turn left on a red light?
options: a:When traveling on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street after stopping.,b:When on a two-way turning onto a two-way after stopping.,c:Whenever traffic is light.,d:Never under any circumstances.
note: After a complete stop, a left turn on red is allowed only from a one-way street onto another one-way street, unless prohibited by signs.

question: If your car begins to skid, how should you react?
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Stay off the brakes and steer to regain control.,c:Apply maximum braking force.,d:Turn off the engine immediately.
note: If the vehicle skids, avoid braking; steer gradually in the direction needed to regain control until traction is restored.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must drivers turning left yield to?
options: a:Oncoming cars.,b:Overtaking cars.,c:No one.
note: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians until it is safe to turn.

question: When driving on a dimly lit street at night, how should you drive?
options: a:Slow enough to stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.,b:Turn on your high beam headlights to better see ahead.,c:Keep the instrument panel lights bright to be more visible to other drivers.
note: Drive at a speed that allows you to stop within the distance lit by your headlights so you can avoid hazards in time.

question: How should you follow a large truck on the freeway?
options: a:No more than one car length behind.,b:Farther behind than when following a passenger car.,c:Closely behind in bad weather.,d:Directly beside the truck.
note: Give extra following distance behind large trucks because they have larger blind spots and require more stopping distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left at an upcoming corner, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Only to oncoming vehicles also turning left.,b:To all approaching vehicles.,c:To pedestrians who are crossing or have the Walk signal.
note: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians in the crosswalk or those with the walk signal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: May you drive off the paved roadway to pass another vehicle?
options: a:If the vehicle ahead is turning left.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:If there are two or more lanes in your direction.,d:If the shoulder is paved and wide.
note: You may not drive off the paved or main-traveled portion of the road (onto the shoulder) to pass another vehicle.

question: How do defensive drivers think about others on the road?
options: a:They know other drivers will do the right thing.,b:They consider what other drivers might do and are prepared to react.,c:They expect no breaks and give none.
note: Defensive drivers anticipate potential mistakes by others and stay ready to respond to unexpected actions.

question: What are blind spots?
options: a:Areas not visible in your vehicle's mirrors.,b:Spots in your vision when tired.,c:Traffic control devices.,d:The rearview mirror view.
note: Blind spots are areas near the rear corners of your vehicle that cannot be seen using mirrors and require a shoulder check.

question: What color are traffic control devices in construction and maintenance areas?
options: a:Yellow.,b:Red.,c:Orange.,d:Green.
note: Orange signs, cones, and barriers indicate work zones; exercise extra caution when you see orange devices.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking downhill, how should you position your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road.,b:Keep your wheels straight.,c:Turn your wheels away from the side of the road.
note: When parking downhill, turn the front wheels toward the curb or roadside so the vehicle will roll into the curb if it moves.

question: What can tailgating other drivers cause?
options: a:Reduce collisions.,b:Frustrate other drivers and increase danger.,c:Prevent passing.,d:Improve traffic flow.
note: Tailgating is aggressive and can provoke anger or unsafe reactions; it increases the risk of a crash and may be illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive markedly slower than surrounding traffic, what is likely to happen?
options: a:Interfere with traffic and receive a ticket.,b:Demonstrate defensive driving techniques.,c:Improve traffic flow.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow can block traffic and may lead to a citation; match traffic speed when safe and legal.

question: Before driving, how much of the vehicle's windows should you clear of snow, frost, and ice?
options: a:Just the windshield.,b:All windows.,c:Just the windshield and passenger window.
note: Clear all snow, ice, and frost from all windows and mirrors so you have unobstructed views before you start driving.

question: When weather or reduced visibility requires headlights, which should you use?
options: a:Use your parking lights.,b:Use your high beams.,c:Use your low beams.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, snow, or other reduced visibility conditions. High beams can reflect off precipitation and reduce visibility.

question: As you approach the top of a hill, how should you drive?
options: a:Maintain a steady speed.,b:Prepare to stop if necessary.,c:Speed up slightly.,d:Move into the left lane.
note: You may not see hazards just beyond the crest. Adjust your speed as you approach a hill so you can stop if there is a stalled vehicle or other obstruction on the roadway.

question: What is the typical color and shape of construction zone signs?
options: a:Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.,b:Round or octagonal with black and yellow coloring.,c:Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.
note: Temporary work-zone and construction signs use an orange background with black symbols or lettering.

question: Why should you look farther ahead on a freeway than on a city street?
options: a:To see potential hazards earlier.,b:Because it takes a quarter-mile to stop.,c:Because it helps you keep up with traffic.
note: On freeways, higher speeds require that you scan further ahead to detect changing traffic conditions, merging vehicles, and potential hazards sooner.

question: Which statement is true about drugs and driving?
options: a:Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.,b:Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.,c:Any prescription drug is safe to use if you don't feel drowsy.
note: Both prescription and over-the-counter medications can impair driving ability; never drive if a drug affects your alertness or coordination.

question: To whom must you give the right-of-way when they are crossing the street?
options: a:Only if they are in a marked crosswalk.,b:Only pedestrians near traffic lights.,c:Pedestrians in any marked or unmarked crosswalk or intersection.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing in marked or unmarked crosswalks and should yield to people crossing any street to ensure safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?
options: a:When the other driver signals you to return.,b:When you see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:After three seconds of signaling.,d:When you pass the other vehicle's front bumper.
note: Return to your lane when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your inside rearview mirror, indicating adequate space.

question: When bicycles are ridden on roadways, they are legally considered what?
options: a:Hazards.,b:Dangerous.,c:Vehicles.
note: Bicycles used on roadways are treated as vehicles. Bicyclists must follow the same rules of the road as motorists and motorists must treat them accordingly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time and the other vehicle is on your left, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on your left has the right-of-way.,b:You have the right-of-way.,c:Whoever is signaling to make a turn has the right-of-way.
note: At a simultaneous arrival at a four-way stop, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. If the other vehicle is on your left, you are to its right and may go first.

question: At a railroad crossing, which precautions should you take?
options: a:Watch for multiple trains.,b:Watch for vehicles that must stop at all railroad crossings (school buses, trucks with hazardous materials).,c:Both of the above.
note: Approach railroad crossings with caution, watch for trains from both directions, and be aware of vehicles that must stop at crossings.

question: Which describes defensive driving behavior?
options: a:Putting one car length between you and the car ahead.,b:Looking only at the car directly in front of you.,c:Keeping your eyes moving to scan for possible hazards.
note: Defensive driving involves scanning the road continuously for hazards, maintaining space, and anticipating others' actions.

question: What defines a crosswalk?
options: a:An area where pedestrians may cross the roadway.,b:Another name for a four-way intersection.,c:An area designated for road construction workers.,d:Only marked white lines between sidewalks.
note: A crosswalk is the area where pedestrians cross the road; it can be marked or unmarked and is protected by right-of-way rules.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another vehicle passes you in a no-passing zone, how should you react?
options: a:Pull off the road.,b:Maintain your speed and position.,c:Slow down and let the other driver safely return to the drive lane.
note: Allow the passing vehicle to return to the lane safely by slowing and providing space so everyone can avoid hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving in the center lane of an expressway and are continually passed on both sides, what should you do?
options: a:Stay in the center lane.,b:Move to the lane on your right.,c:Move to the lane on your left.
note: On multi-lane roads, drive in the right lanes unless passing or turning left. Move right if traffic is passing you on both sides.

question: Why is using a cell phone while driving considered a distraction?
options: a:It occupies the driver's hands, eyes, and mind.,b:It draws attention of other drivers.,c:It costs money.,d:It improves communication while driving.
note: Cell phone use diverts your hands, eyes, and attention from driving, greatly increasing crash risk.

question: Which of the following is the correct way to operate the accelerator and brake pedals?
options: a:Use your left foot to brake.,b:Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating your vehicle.,c:You should always brake abruptly to ensure stopping.
note: Use your right foot for both the accelerator and brake. Apply brakes smoothly with increasing pressure for a controlled stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle traveling in the same direction, how should you pass?
options: a:Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.,b:Pass the vehicle as slowly as possible.,c:Pass as safely and as quickly as possible.
note: Pass quickly and safely so you regain full visibility; return to your lane when you can see the other vehicle's headlights in your mirror.

question: What is the correct top-to-bottom order of traffic signal lights?
options: a:Green, red, yellow.,b:Red, yellow, green.,c:Red, green, yellow.
note: The standard vertical order from top to bottom is red, yellow, then green.

question: Signs with orange backgrounds are used to indicate what?
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Construction and maintenance warning signs.,c:General warning signs.
note: Orange signs are used specifically for construction and maintenance warnings to alert drivers of temporary conditions.

question: When should you use your high-beam headlights while driving at night?
options: a:When there are no oncoming vehicles approaching.,b:When you are following another vehicle in heavy traffic.,c:When you are within a one-block distance of an oncoming vehicle.
note: Use high beams on unlit open roads to increase visibility. Dim to low beams at least 500 feet before meeting oncoming vehicles and within 300 feet when following another vehicle.

question: When taking any medication, what should you do regarding driving?
options: a:Keep your window open and drive more slowly.,b:Have someone follow you home.,c:Consult your doctor or pharmacist about effects before driving.
note: Prescription and over-the-counter medicines can impair driving. Consult your doctor or pharmacist about how a drug may affect your ability to drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian crosses your lane, what should you do?
options: a:Cautiously drive around them.,b:Make sure the pedestrian sees you then proceed.,c:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.,d:Honk and continue.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway even where no marked crosswalk exists; stop and allow them to cross.

question: What is the crash risk effect of a BAC of 0.02 percent?
options: a:It won't affect your driving.,b:It won't put other drivers at risk.,c:It will nearly double your chances of having an accident.
note: Even small increases in BAC significantly raise crash risk. Each 0.02 percent increase nearly doubles the risk of a fatal crash.

question: When passing a line of parked cars, what should you be prepared for?
options: a:Be prepared for a person or vehicle to unexpectedly enter your lane.,b:Expect all other drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.,c:Drive closely to the parked vehicles to allow more room for moving traffic.
note: People can step out from between parked cars or a vehicle may pull out; give extra space and be prepared to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under which condition may you pass another vehicle?
options: a:You are on a hill or curve.,b:You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.,c:You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
note: You may pass when the line next to your lane is broken, indicating passing is permitted if it is safe to do so.

question: What action will cause the MVA to suspend a driver's license related to testing?
options: a:Refusing to submit to a BAC or drug test.,b:Submitting to a breath test.,c:Using a fake ID to buy alcohol.,d:Failing a field sobriety test only.
note: If a driver refuses a certified chemical test when requested by police, the MVA will impose a suspension for test refusal under implied consent laws.

question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, how should you wear it?
options: a:Only the lap belt.,b:Both the lap and shoulder belts.,c:Only the shoulder belt.,d:None if airbags are present.
note: Use both the lap and shoulder belts together to maximize protection; using only one part greatly reduces effectiveness.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do about the brakes?
options: a:Brake abruptly.,b:Stay off the brakes.,c:Brake lightly.
note: Do not apply the brakes during most skids; steer in the direction of the skid and regain control before braking.

question: As you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light, what should you do?
options: a:Stop before crossing the intersection.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Wait for a green light before proceeding.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution, watching for cross traffic and pedestrians.

question: When are large trucks likely to lose speed?
options: a:Driving up long or steep hills.,b:Driving down long, gradual hills.,c:Driving in long gradual curves.,d:Driving on level surfaces.
note: Trucks often slow on long or steep uphill grades because of their size and load, so give them extra space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal is not working, what should you do at the intersection?
options: a:If the intersection is clear, you may not need to stop.,b:Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.,c:Drive quickly through the intersection to get out of the way of other vehicles.
note: When lights are out, treat the intersection as an all-way stop: come to a complete stop and yield to vehicles and pedestrians according to right-of-way rules.

question: Why should you look far ahead while driving on the highway?
options: a:Helps you keep up with traffic.,b:Reduces the need for last-minute braking or turning.,c:Allows you to spot upcoming police officers.
note: Looking far ahead gives you time to react, reduces the need for sudden maneuvers, and helps maintain smooth traffic flow.

question: When parking uphill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn the front wheels?
options: a:Straight ahead.,b:Toward the right, toward the side of the road.,c:Toward the left, toward the center of the road.
note: On hills without a curb, turn wheels so that if the vehicle rolls, it moves away from the center of the road (toward the edge).

question: Which is a dangerous habit when driving in work zones?
options: a:Tailgating another vehicle.,b:Failing to watch for workers and moving equipment.,c:Both of the above.
note: Work zones present unique hazards; tailgating and not watching for workers or equipment greatly increase the risk of collisions.

question: Which statement best describes backing up a vehicle?
options: a:Always dangerous.,b:Dangerous if you have a helper.,c:Only dangerous in large vehicles.
note: Backing up is inherently risky because visibility is limited; use extra caution and assistance when available.

question: If you see animals standing near the roadway, you should:
options: a:Quickly swerve into the next lane.,b:Speed up to scare them away.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: Animals near the road may bolt unpredictably. Slow down and be alert for more animals that may be out of sight.

question: Which statement about blind spots is true?
options: a:Blind spots are eliminated with one outside mirror.,b:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than passenger vehicles.,c:Blind spots can be checked by looking in the rearview mirror.,d:Blind spots do not exist on modern vehicles.
note: Even with proper mirrors, vehicles have blind spots; large trucks have much larger blind zones than passenger cars.

question: When is it necessary to use your low beam headlights?
options: a:On a lighted street.,b:On a freeway.,c:In fog.
note: Use low beams in fog, rain, snow, or whenever visibility is reduced; high beams may worsen glare.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, to whom should you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on your left.,b:Anyone who arrived before you.,c:The driver across from your vehicle.
note: Vehicles proceed through a four-way stop in the order they arrived. Yield to any driver who arrived earlier than you.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, what should you do first?
options: a:Stop.,b:Turn back onto the roadway immediately.,c:Wait until it is safe, then gradually re-enter the roadway.
note: Do not jerk the wheel back onto the road. Slow down, check traffic, and re-enter gradually when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to enter a freeway but see no gap in traffic, what should you do on the ramp?
options: a:Stop at the end of the ramp to wait for a gap.,b:Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.,c:Maintain your speed and force other drivers to create a gap.
note: If no gap is available, slow down on the acceleration ramp to wait for a safe space to merge; do not stop at the ramp end unless necessary.

question: Which type of road surface tends to freeze first?
options: a:A tunnel.,b:An intersection.,c:A bridge.
note: Bridges and overpasses are exposed to air on all sides and often freeze before adjoining roadways, even when other pavement is dry.

question: What is considered a distraction while driving?
options: a:Anything that makes you pay more attention to driving.,b:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,c:Only cell phone use.,d:Only passengers making noise.
note: A distraction is any activity or object that diverts your eyes, hands, or mind from driving and increases crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering traffic from a curb, what should you do?
options: a:Drive more slowly than traffic for 200 feet.,b:Wait for a large enough gap to reach the speed of traffic.,c:Pull directly into the first available gap.,d:Stop and back into traffic if needed.
note: Merge only when there is a gap large enough for your vehicle to accelerate to the speed of traffic safely.

question: What color and lettering do temporary construction and maintenance signs use?
options: a:Red background with green writing.,b:Orange background with black writing.,c:Yellow background with blue writing.
note: Temporary work zone signs use an orange background with black text or symbols to warn drivers of construction and maintenance activities.

question: When parking on any hill, which practice should you follow?
options: a:One rear wheel should touch the curb.,b:Use the parking brake and leave the car in park.,c:Leave the front wheels parallel to the road if a curb exists.,d:Leave the vehicle in neutral.
note: Always set the parking brake and leave the vehicle in 'park' (or in gear for manual transmissions) when parked on a hill.

question: When following a motorcycle, how should you adjust your following distance?
options: a:Be ready to use your horn.,b:Drive more slowly.,c:Allow a larger following distance.
note: Motorcycles can stop more quickly and are harder to see; maintain at least a three- to four-second following distance.

question: How can you avoid headlight glare from an approaching car?
options: a:Look briefly toward the right side of the road.,b:Keep focused on the centerline.,c:Flash your high beams.,d:Stare straight ahead.
note: Glance toward the right edge of the roadway to avoid being blinded by oncoming headlights while maintaining lane position.

question: When driving at night, what should you do to improve safety?
options: a:Always use your high beams.,b:Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: Increase following distance at night to allow more reaction time; use high beams only when appropriate and avoid staring at oncoming headlights.

question: When must you present proof of insurance to law enforcement?
options: a:Only if you are involved in a collision.,b:If you are involved in a collision or stopped for a citation.,c:Only if you are stopped and cited.
note: You must carry evidence of financial responsibility and present proof of insurance to an officer upon request after a stop or collision.

question: As your speed increases, what becomes more important?
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Look well ahead of your vehicle.,c:Change lanes frequently.
note: At higher speeds, look farther ahead to spot hazards early and allow adequate reaction distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching an octagonal (eight-sided) sign, what must you do?
options: a:Turn.,b:Stop.,c:Slow.
note: An octagonal sign always means STOP: come to a complete stop, yield as required, and proceed when safe.

question: Which of the following commonly contributes to traffic crashes?
options: a:Getting adequate rest and staying alert.,b:Scanning the environment and staying focused on the driving task.,c:Exceeding the posted speed limit and driving too fast for conditions or circumstances.
note: Driving faster than the posted limit or too fast for conditions is a common cause of crashes. Safe driving involves matching conditions and the flow of traffic.

question: What should you do when driving through a work zone?
options: a:Maintain your normal speed.,b:Increase speed to clear the zone quickly.,c:Reduce speed and be prepared to stop.,d:Ignore lane markings in the zone.
note: Slow down, obey posted limits, and be prepared to stop in work zones; workers and equipment may be present.

question: What can you do to help reduce road rage incidents?
options: a:Always signal your intention when changing lanes.,b:Use your horn frequently.,c:Talk on your cell phone while driving.
note: Signal intentions, follow traffic laws, and be courteous to reduce confrontations and road rage.

question: A vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you and creates a hazard. What should you do first?
options: a:Honk and step on the brake firmly.,b:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,c:Swerve into the lane next to you.
note: Remove your foot from the accelerator to increase the space between you and the vehicle ahead; avoid sudden braking or swerving if possible.

question: How can you help keep the driver behind you a safe distance away?
options: a:Driving 10 mph faster than the car behind you.,b:Driving 10 mph slower than the car behind you.,c:Maintaining a steady speed.
note: Maintaining a steady speed and signaling properly encourages safe following distance from drivers behind you.

question: What is hydroplaning?
options: a:The windshield wipers cannot keep the windshield clear of rain.,b:Tires lose contact with the road surface.,c:Spray from a large truck reduces visibility.
note: Hydroplaning occurs when tires ride on a film of water and lose contact with the road, causing partial or total loss of control.

question: Which statement about driving through roadwork zones is true?
options: a:Fines are the same for violations in work zones as under normal conditions.,b:You must "Slow for the Cone Zone.",c:Only slow down if you think workers are present.
note: Drive carefully and slow down in work zones. Many jurisdictions enforce increased fines in marked work areas and promote the "Slow for the Cone Zone" message.

question: Which statements about driving speed are true?
options: a:As your speed increases, the chance of a fatality increases.,b:As your speed increases, so should your following distance.,c:Both of the above.
note: Higher speeds increase crash severity; increase following distance as speed increases to allow safe stopping.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, you should be driving:
options: a:At the legal speed limit.,b:More slowly than the freeway traffic.,c:At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.
note: Enter the freeway at or near the speed of traffic so you can merge smoothly; do not merge at a much slower speed.

question: At dawn, dusk, or in rain or snow when visibility is poor, what is a good way to let others know you are present?
options: a:Turn up the instrumental panel lights.,b:Turn on your parking lights.,c:Turn on your headlights.
note: Use your headlights in low-visibility conditions so other drivers can see you; low beams are appropriate when wipers are required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must drivers obey directions given by flaggers at road works?
options: a:Security guards patrolling parking lots.,b:Other drivers whose vehicles are broken down on the roadway.,c:Flaggers (signal persons) at construction sites.
note: Flaggers give directions to maintain safety in work zones. Drivers must follow their instructions and posted work-zone signs.

question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is correct?
options: a:If you can walk in a straight line, it's safe to drive.,b:If under the legal BAC limit, your driving isn't impaired.,c:Alcohol affects judgment needed for safe driving.,d:Alcohol only impairs at high concentrations.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment and decision-making necessary for safe driving; even small amounts can be dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you check freeway traffic before entering?
options: a:Using your rearview mirror.,b:Using your rearview and side mirrors.,c:Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.
note: Use side mirrors and a shoulder check to cover blind spots and ensure it is safe to merge onto the freeway.

question: If you want to pass a pedestrian walking along the road and an oncoming vehicle is approaching, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.,b:Honk your horn to make the pedestrian move over.,c:Keep driving at the same speed; the oncoming vehicle must yield.,d:Stop and wait until the roadway is completely clear.
note: When facing multiple hazards, handle one at a time. If an oncoming vehicle is approaching, slow and let it pass, then pass the pedestrian only if it is safe.

question: When are streets and highways most slippery?
options: a:When it has been raining hard for several hours.,b:When they are clean and dry.,c:Just after it starts to rain.
note: Roadways are especially slippery when rain first begins because water mixes with oil and residues on the pavement.

question: When following another vehicle at night, which headlights should you use?
options: a:High beams.,b:Parking lights.,c:Low beams.,d:Fog lights.
note: When following another vehicle within about 300 feet, use low beam headlights to avoid reducing the other driver's visibility from glare in their mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How can you check for vehicles in your blind spots?
options: a:The inside rearview mirror.,b:The outside rearview mirror.,c:By looking over your shoulder.
note: Blind spots cannot be seen by mirrors alone. Turn your head and glance over the appropriate shoulder before changing lanes.

question: If poor weather reduces your visibility, what should you do regarding following distance?
options: a:Speed up to get off the road quickly.,b:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: Increase following distance in poor visibility to give yourself more time to react to sudden stops or hazards you may not see immediately.

question: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, when may vehicles behind it proceed?
options: a:When all students are off the bus.,b:When the stop arm is retracted.,c:When the stop arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion.
note: Do not move until the bus turns off the flashing lights, the stop arm is withdrawn, and the bus starts moving again. Ensure no children are crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before returning to your original lane after passing, what should you confirm?
options: a:Beep your horn.,b:See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:Flash your headlights.
note: Only move back into the lane when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror and it's safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it acceptable to start across an intersection if you will block it when the light turns red?
options: a:Under any circumstances.,b:Unless you entered the intersection on a yellow light.,c:Unless you entered the intersection on a green light.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless you can fully clear it before the light turns red; never enter if you will block cross traffic.

question: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Call your insurance company when you get home.,b:Wait for the owner to return.,c:Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.
note: If you damage a parked vehicle and the owner is not present, leave a note with your contact information securely attached and report it if required.

question: How should you change speed and direction on snowy or icy roads?
options: a:Use cruise control to maintain speed.,b:Make speed and directional changes more gradually.,c:Drive as you would on dry pavement.,d:Brake suddenly to test traction.
note: On snow or ice, make gradual speed and steering adjustments and never use cruise control to avoid loss of control.

question: What should you do if you become drowsy while driving?
options: a:Try to fight it and keep driving.,b:Take a break and rest.,c:Take caffeine pills and continue.,d:Drive with cruise control.
note: If drowsy, stop at the next rest area or safe location to rest or change drivers; rest is the only effective remedy.

question: What does a five-sided (pentagon) traffic sign indicate?
options: a:Stop sign.,b:Regulatory sign.,c:School zone or school crossing sign.
note: A pentagon-shaped sign warns drivers they are entering a school zone or a school crossing area where children may be present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If there's no marked crosswalk and you see a pedestrian crossing your lane, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and carefully pass.,b:Make eye contact then pass.,c:Stop and allow the pedestrian to finish crossing.,d:Honk to warn them.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing the road even where no crosswalk is marked; stop and allow them to cross safely.

question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use your turn signals?
options: a:Only when pulling away from the curb.,b:When pulling next to the curb but not away.,c:When pulling next to or away from the curb.
note: Signal both when pulling toward a curb and when pulling away so other drivers and pedestrians understand your intentions.

question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,b:Stop if you are driving in the same direction.,c:Stop, regardless of your direction of travel.
note: When a school bus is stopped to board or discharge children with lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must stop in all directions unless oncoming lanes are separated by a physical divider.

question: It is unsafe for a child under what age to ride in the front seat of a passenger vehicle?
note: Children under age 13 should ride properly restrained in the rear seat for best protection, especially because front-seat airbags can be dangerous for young children.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the effect of continually passing vehicles on a two-lane road?
options: a:It increases your chances of a collision.,b:It helps prevent congestion.,c:Gets you more quickly and safely to your destination.,d:It is always legal.
note: Frequent passing on two-lane roads raises collision risk; avoid unnecessary passing and drive defensively.

question: What does a steady green traffic light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Increase your speed.,b:Adjust your mirrors.,c:You may proceed through the intersection at a safe speed if it is clear.
note: A steady green means you may go if the intersection is clear; yield to those already in the intersection or to pedestrians.

question: What does the abbreviation 'BAC' mean?
options: a:Blood alcohol concentration.,b:Blood alcohol conservation.,c:Big alcohol content.
note: BAC stands for blood alcohol concentration and measures the percentage of alcohol in the bloodstream.

question: A large truck ahead is turning right onto a two-lane street. What should you expect?
options: a:May complete its turn in either of the two lanes.,b:May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.,c:Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.
note: Long vehicles often need to swing wide to make turns because their rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels.

question: What is the best response if you become tired while driving?
options: a:Stop to rest or change drivers.,b:Open a window and keep driving.,c:Drink coffee and drive on.,d:Turn on loud music to stay awake.
note: If tired, stop and rest, nap, or switch drivers; caffeine and windows are not reliable substitutes for sleep.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Turn into any lane.,b:Turn into the first lane.,c:Turn into the second lane.
note: When turning from a two-way to a one-way street, turn into the first available legal lane in the direction you’re traveling.

question: If your car is equipped with airbags, what is the rule about seat belts?
options: a:Seat belts do not need to be worn.,b:Seat belts should be worn behind the back.,c:Seat belts should still be worn.
note: Airbags are supplemental restraint systems; for full protection, lap and shoulder belts must still be worn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes, besides checking your mirrors, what else should you do?
options: a:Never look over your right shoulder.,b:Always slow down in your traffic lane.,c:Glance over your shoulder to check blind spots.
note: Always check mirrors and look over your shoulder to verify that the lane is clear of vehicles in your blind spots before you change lanes.

question: What does a broken (dashed) yellow line between two lanes of traffic indicate?
options: a:Both lanes of traffic are going in the same direction.,b:Passing is permitted when it's safe.,c:Passing is not permitted.
note: A dashed yellow line separates opposing traffic and indicates passing is allowed when it is safe and clear of oncoming traffic.

question: If you are under 21, at what BAC can your license be suspended for driving?
options: a:0.08 percent or more.,b:0.08 percent or more.,c:Any amount.
note: Maryland enforces zero tolerance for drivers under 21: any detectable amount of alcohol can lead to license suspension.

question: Why should you frequently check your rearview mirrors?
options: a:Only when you are slowing down.,b:To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.,c:Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
note: Regularly checking rearview mirrors helps you monitor traffic around you and anticipate situations that may require action.

question: If you are about to be hit from the rear, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Applying your brakes.,b:Letting go of the steering wheel.,c:Pressing your head against the head restraint.
note: If struck from behind, keep a firm grip on the wheel and press your head against the head restraint. Do not let go of the steering wheel.

question: What must you do when approaching a stopped school bus with flashing lights and an extended signal arm?
options: a:Proceed at 15 mph if no children are visible.,b:Stop and remain stopped until the arm is retracted.,c:Slow and pass carefully.,d:Honk and pass quickly.
note: Stop and remain stopped for a school bus with flashing lights and extended arm until the bus resumes motion and the arm is withdrawn.

question: A pedestrian with a guide dog is waiting to cross as you make a right turn. What should you do?
options: a:Turn off your engine until the person crosses.,b:Tell the pedestrian when to cross the street.,c:Wait until the person has crossed before turning.
note: Pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes are blind or visually impaired and must be given the right-of-way. Wait until they have safely crossed.

question: What are "no zones" around large trucks?
options: a:Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or limit the truck's ability to maneuver safely.,b:Places with plenty of room to follow a truck, c:Zones where several car lengths separate you from the truck.
note: "No zones" are the large blind-spot areas around trucks and buses where other vehicles may disappear from the driver's view or restrict the truck's stopping and turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering the interstate, after checking for a gap and signaling you should:
options: a:Expect traffic to allow you to proceed into the lane, since you have the right-of-way.,b:Wait for the lane to clear before merging.,c:Merge carefully into the gap.
note: Identify a gap, accelerate to match traffic speed, signal, and merge carefully when it is safe—do not assume other drivers will yield.

question: How can sudden wind gusts affect vehicles on highways?
options: a:They only affect large vehicles.,b:They can cause problems for all vehicles.,c:They only reduce visibility.,d:They only affect parked cars.
note: Strong wind gusts can affect vehicles of all sizes by altering stability and reducing visibility due to blowing debris.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol or drug use?
options: a:Alertness and concentration.,b:Reaction time and coordination.,c:All of the above.
note: Alcohol and many drugs reduce alertness and concentration and slow reaction time, impairing coordination and driving ability.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct procedure for making a right turn?
options: a:Signal, slow down, and get into the lane closest to the centerline before turning.,b:Signal, slow down, and get into the lane closest to the right curb before turning.,c:Approach in the lane nearest the right curb but move toward the center before turning.
note: Before a right turn, signal, slow down, and approach from the lane nearest the right curb, staying as close as practical to the curb or edge of the roadway.

question: In traffic moving at 50–55 mph, how are you least likely to have an accident?
options: a:Drive a few miles per hour faster than most other vehicles.,b:Drive a few miles per hour slower than most other vehicles.,c:Stay within that speed range as other traffic does.
note: Traveling smoothly with the flow of traffic within posted limits reduces speed differentials and collision risk.

question: What is an important step to take when making a turn?
options: a:Always move to the left lane.,b:Increase your speed.,c:Check traffic in all directions.
note: Before turning, check mirrors and look for traffic, pedestrians, and cyclists in all directions to ensure the turn is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you enter a roundabout, what must you yield to?
options: a:Pedestrians and bicyclists crossing and traffic already in the roundabout.,b:Cars approaching from the left only.,c:Only vehicles, not pedestrians.,d:No one; you have the right-of-way.
note: Yield to any pedestrians or bicyclists at the crosswalk and to vehicles already circulating in the roundabout.

question: If the centerline has one solid yellow and one broken yellow with the broken next to your lane, what does it mean?
options: a:You are in a no-pass zone.,b:You may pass from your lane if clear.,c:You may only make right turns.,d:You must stop before passing.
note: A broken yellow line next to your lane means you may pass on the left when it is safe and no oncoming traffic is present.

question: How many alcoholic drinks are required to begin affecting your driving ability?
options: a:One,b:Two,c:Three
note: Even a single drink can impair coordination and judgment; it is not safe to drive after any alcohol consumption.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When can you safely move back into the right lane after passing a vehicle going the same direction?
options: a:After about three seconds.,b:When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.,c:When you can see the entire front (both headlights) of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: Do not return to your lane until you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror; also check blind spots before moving over.

question: If a school bus ahead on your side of the road has red lights flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Slow to a speed no faster than 10 mph.,b:Change lanes and pass cautiously.,c:Stop until the lights stop flashing.
note: When a school bus is stopped with red flashing lights and its stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is retracted.

question: In which situation should your wheels NOT be pointed straight ahead?
options: a:When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.,b:When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.,c:When parked on a level roadway with no curb.
note: When parked on a slope, turn your wheels so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail. Keep wheels straight when stopped awaiting a left turn.

question: When is driving permitted under the influence of medication that impairs you?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:If you don't feel drowsy.,c:If prescribed by a physician.,d:If it's over-the-counter.
note: It is illegal and unsafe to drive under the influence of any medication that impairs your ability to operate a vehicle.

question: Which lights should drivers use to improve visibility in rain or fog?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: Low beam headlights help you see and help others see you in rain or fog. High beams will reflect and reduce visibility; parking lights are insufficient.

question: At a school crossing sign, what should drivers do?
options: a:Always stop whether a stop sign is present or not.,b:Watch for children and be ready to stop.,c:Always sound your horn when you see children.
note: A pentagonal school crossing sign warns you that children may be present. Slow and be prepared to stop when you see these signs.

question: How should you respond to an aggressive driver?
options: a:Challenge them.,b:Get out of their way.,c:Speed up to pass them.,d:Make obscene gestures.
note: Avoid confrontation by safely getting out of the aggressive driver's path; do not engage or escalate the situation.

question: If your vehicle begins to hydroplane, what should you do?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly to prevent sliding.,b:Drive at a constant speed to gain better traction.,c:Slow down gradually and avoid using the brakes.
note: If hydroplaning occurs, ease off the accelerator, steer straight, and slow gently without braking hard until traction returns.

question: What does a broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:A construction zone is ahead.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:Passing is permitted when the way is clear.
note: A broken yellow centerline allows passing from either direction when it is safe and there is no oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a red light with a green arrow, when are you permitted to proceed in the arrow's direction?
options: a:You must first come to a complete stop.,b:You must wait until the light changes.,c:If you are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear, you may go.
note: A green arrow authorizes movement in the arrow's direction if you are in the correct lane and yield to anyone already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is a U-turn explicitly prohibited?
options: a:In a parking lot.,b:On or near any curve or hill.,c:On a straight road with clear view for 500 feet.
note: Do not make U-turns on or near curves or hills where oncoming traffic cannot see you in time to avoid a collision.

question: If a school bus is stopped ahead loading or unloading children with lights flashing and stop arm extended, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop until all the children have left the bus.,b:Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.,c:Change lanes, slow, and pass cautiously.
note: When a school bus displays flashing red lights and the stop arm is extended, stop and remain stopped until the lights are off and the stop arm withdrawn. Be alert for children crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you respond to a funeral procession?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to vehicles in the procession.,b:Drive between procession vehicles.,c:Pass on the right at high speed.,d:Ignore the procession entirely.
note: Other vehicles must yield to vehicles in a funeral procession until all have passed, even if you have a green signal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Within an intersection where there are no oncoming vehicles.,b:Wherever signs and/or pavement markings permit passing.,c:Within a curve where there are no oncoming vehicles.
note: Only pass where signs and pavement markings allow it, and ensure you have enough space and clear sight to complete the maneuver safely.

question: Where is the safest place for children age 12 and under in a vehicle with airbags?
options: a:The bed of a pickup truck.,b:The front seat.,c:The back seat.,d:Standing on the floorboard.
note: Children 12 and under should ride in the back seat because airbags can cause severe injury to young passengers.

question: When double solid yellow lines separate lanes of traffic, what is true about passing?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the left.,b:Passing is permitted from the right.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate opposing traffic; passing is prohibited in both directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, what should you not do?
options: a:Back up on the road or shoulder.,b:Continue to the next exit.,c:Find an alternate route.,d:Proceed to the next crossroad.
note: Never back up on a highway; continue to the next exit and re-route safely.

question: How should you follow a large truck on the roadway?
options: a:Closer than when following a passenger car.,b:Farther behind than when following a passenger car.,c:To the right to pass quickly.,d:Directly beside the truck's blind spot.
note: Maintain a greater following distance behind large trucks to see around them and allow extra braking space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto an interstate highway, what is the correct action?
options: a:Select a safe gap and merge into the lane of traffic.,b:Merge across two lanes at once.,c:Always stop before entering the highway.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic, find a safe gap, and merge smoothly into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you plan to pass another vehicle, what should you not assume?
options: a:That the other driver will make space for you to return.,b:That signaling makes passing illegal.,c:That they will slow down.,d:That they will always keep speed constant.
note: Do not assume another driver will make room for your pass even if you signal; ensure the lane is clear and safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering an interstate from an on-ramp, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and check for cars before entering.,b:Check for cars and reduce your speed to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.,c:Check for cars, increase speed to match the flow, and merge when safe.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic on the freeway and merge smoothly when a safe gap appears. Do not stop on the ramp.

question: How can you reduce the chance of skidding on slippery surfaces?
options: a:Speed up before entering curves.,b:Shift to a higher gear going down steep hills.,c:Slow down before entering curves and intersections.,d:Brake hard during the curve.
note: Reduce speed before curves and intersections on slippery roads; avoid sudden braking or steering that causes skids.

question: What is the purpose of work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs?
options: a:To keep traffic out of hazardous work zones.,b:To inconvenience drivers.,c:To make drivers angry about delays.,d:To mark detours only.
note: Work zone devices protect workers and guide drivers away from hazardous areas; obey them and reduce speed.

question: A diamond-shaped road sign generally indicates what?
options: a:Stop.,b:Warning of special conditions or hazards ahead.,c:Yield.,d:Regulatory requirements.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs used to alert drivers to special conditions or hazards ahead. They are typically yellow (or orange in work zones).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you exit the freeway on a ramp that curves downhill, what should you do before entering the curve?
options: a:Slow to a safe speed before the curve.,b:Slow to the posted freeway speed limit.,c:Wait until you are in the curve to begin braking.
note: Reduce your speed before you enter the curve; braking while in the curve can cause skids and loss of control.

question: What is the best definition of distracted driving?
options: a:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,b:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,c:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.
note: Distracted driving includes anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind off driving, and is a common cause of collisions.

question: What should you do when driving at night to increase safety?
options: a:Always use your high beams.,b:Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: Lower visibility reduces your ability to judge distances and speeds at night—leave more space between you and the vehicle ahead.

question: If your vehicle develops a mechanical problem on the road, what should you do?
options: a:Stop in your lane and put on your hazard lights.,b:Signal and pull into the slow lane.,c:Put on your hazard lights and pull off the road.
note: Get the vehicle off the traveled portion of the road if possible and turn on emergency flashers so other drivers can see you.

question: If you are already inside an intersection when a green light turns yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Increase your speed so as not to cause an accident.,b:Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.,c:Stop immediately in the intersection.
note: If you are already in the intersection when the light changes to yellow, proceed to clear it safely rather than stopping in the middle.

question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?
options: a:Relax and concentrate on safe driving.,b:Tailgate slower drivers.,c:Drive above posted speed limits.,d:Honk repeatedly to move traffic.
note: Prevent aggressive driving by staying calm, keeping realistic travel times, obeying laws, and not taking others' actions personally.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left at an intersection, to whom must you yield?
options: a:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:No one in particular.,c:Oncoming traffic should yield to you.
note: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians until it is safe to complete the turn.

question: If you are driving next to a single broken white line on a highway, what does it allow?
options: a:You cannot cross the line to pass.,b:You may cross the line to pass or change lanes.,c:You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; you may cross them to change lanes or pass when safe.

question: Which substance slows reaction time and impairs judgment leading to slower reactions?
options: a:Working hard.,b:Sleeping.,c:Drinking alcohol.,d:Caffeinated drinks.
note: Alcohol reduces alertness, slows reflexes, impairs distance and speed judgment, and increases crash risk.

question: What does a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line between lanes indicate?
options: a:Passing is permitted from both directions.,b:Passing is permitted only from the direction next to the dashed line.,c:Passing is prohibited from both directions.
note: When a dashed yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, only traffic next to the dashed line may cross the centerline to pass; the lane next to the solid line may not pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you check blind spots when preparing to change lanes?
options: a:Only the left outside mirror.,b:Look over your left or right shoulder.,c:Only the inside rearview mirror.
note: Look over the appropriate shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes; mirrors alone do not show everything.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Four-way flashers.,d:Parking lights only.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog because high beams reflect off moisture and reduce visibility.

question: A driver's license is legally considered which of the following?
options: a:A right you have automatically.,b:A privilege you must earn and maintain.,c:A mandatory requirement for all citizens.
note: A driver's license is a privilege granted by the state; it can be suspended or revoked for violations and must be maintained according to law.

question: When driving in fog, what lighting should you use?
options: a:Slow down and use your low beam headlights.,b:Slow down and use your high beam headlights.,c:Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.
note: Use low beams in fog to reduce glare and slow down; if visibility is extremely poor, pull off the road safely and wait.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach an intersection where your side view is blocked, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and look both ways.,b:Maintain your speed and look both ways.,c:Stop, then inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions.
note: Stop and inch forward slowly until you have a clear view in both directions before proceeding through an intersection with blocked sight lines.

question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?
options: a:Before you start driving.,b:After driving a few minutes.,c:Whenever you think of it.,d:While the car is moving.
note: Adjust mirrors, seat, and fasten your seat belt before moving the vehicle; do not adjust them while driving.

question: Which of the following is true about large trucks?
options: a:They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.,b:They are more maneuverable than passenger vehicles.,c:They all have air brakes that allow them to stop quickly.
note: Large trucks require substantially more stopping distance than passenger cars, especially when fully loaded.

question: Which headlights should you use to improve visibility in rain or fog?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: Use low beam headlights in rain, fog, snow, or sleet. High beams can reflect off precipitation and reduce visibility.

question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, which beam setting should you use?
options: a:High beams until 10 feet away.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.,d:Emergency flashers.
note: Use low beams when following another vehicle at night to avoid blinding the driver ahead.

question: When a traffic signal turns yellow as you approach, what should you do if you can stop safely?
options: a:Speed up to cross the intersection.,b:Slow down and proceed through the intersection without caution.,c:Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.
note: A steady yellow warns the light is changing to red; stop if you can do so safely, otherwise proceed with caution.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim high beams at night, where should you direct your gaze?
options: a:Look straight ahead in your lane.,b:Look toward the left edge of your lane.,c:Look toward the right edge of your lane.
note: If an oncoming vehicle uses high beams, avoid looking directly at the lights. Look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the vehicle using peripheral vision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At intersections with a Yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is near enough to cause conflict.,b:Yield only to vehicles on your right.,c:Always slow down but never stop.
note: Slow or stop as needed at a yield sign and give the right-of-way to traffic close enough to pose a conflict.

question: Collisions are more likely to occur under which condition?
options: a:All vehicles traveling at roughly the same speed.,b:One lane of traffic traveling faster than the other lanes.,c:One vehicle moving faster or slower than the flow of traffic.
note: Crashes are more likely when a vehicle's speed varies considerably from the flow of traffic; driving significantly slower or faster increases collision risk.

question: What is a common effect of excessive speed?
options: a:Increases ability to react.,b:Often leads to high-risk decision-making.,c:Does not change crash risk.,d:Makes driving safer.
note: Excessive speed increases crash risk and often results in poor decision-making; it rarely saves time and is dangerous.

question: Why increase following distance behind large vehicles?
options: a:To better see around the sides of the vehicle.,b:Because large vehicles travel faster.,c:Because of the vehicle's slipstream.,d:To prevent others from cutting in.
note: Large vehicles can block your view and have larger blind spots; increase distance to see around them and provide stopping space.

question: After stopping for a passing train, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Proceed when the gates stop moving.,b:Look for a second train and wait until all signals stop.,c:Cross the tracks as soon as the first train passes.,d:Back up if traffic blocks your way.
note: Watch for another train on adjacent tracks and do not proceed until gates are fully raised and signals have ceased.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you yield your legal right-of-way?
options: a:Often, even at controlled intersections.,b:Whenever it helps prevent collisions.,c:Never — it confuses other drivers.
note: Give up your legal right-of-way when doing so will help avoid a crash. Never assume others will follow right-of-way rules.
